While technically true that no pocket is visible, this is a minor feature. More importantly, the Router correctly identified the presence of text/branding but failed to penalize the *quality* of that branding in the alignment score sufficiently, treating it merely as 'present'. I agree with the testability judgments but disagree with the implication that the 'branding' checkpoint is fully satisfied given the gibberish nature of the text.

All major geometric checkpoints (spine, rings, rectangular shape) are present. However, the alignment is penalized because the 'branding' checkpoint, while technically present, is semantically invalid due to AI-generated gibberish. A real binder would have legible text or a clear logo. The gibberish reduces the semantic fidelity of the 'labeling' attribute.
